targets.title: This number just feels right: the impact of roundedness of price numbers on product evaluations.
targets.evidence_quote:
A pre-registered replication of study 5 from the original article was conducted in a sample of
N
=588 participants. For both the original product and one alternative product neither an interaction between price roundedness and context, nor a mediation through ‘a sense of feeling right’ was found.
targets.outcome_quote: Our results did not unambiguously support the rounded price effect and provide evidence against the proposed mediation. While the descriptive statistics hint in the predicted direction, analyses using significance tests and Bayes factors could not yield strong evidence for the effect, except for a single contrast that was significant. This, however, is only weak evidence in the context of the proposed effect.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central rounded-price interaction and proposed mediation were not supported for either product. Caution that a tiny effect cannot be excluded does not declare the attempt uninformative.

reasoning: Full article and reference list verified by title and four authors. New participant sample retests Wadhwa and Zhang study 5; the earlier O’Donnell and Nelson replication supplies comparison evidence and is not itself retested. Published-statistic p-curve analysis does not reanalyse the original data.
